title: Remove Methods From Project
summary: Given a project with n methods numbered 0 to n-1, and a bug in method k, remove all methods invoked directly or indirectly by k.
statement: Given a project with n methods numbered 0 to n-1, and a bug in method k, remove all methods invoked directly or indirectly by k. A group of methods can only be removed if no external method invokes any within the group. Return an array of remaining methods, in any order, or an empty array if no removal is possible.
constraints: Methods are 0..n-1 and each distinct directed edge [a,b] means a invokes b.
The suspicious set contains k and every method reachable from k.
Remove that entire set only if no outside method invokes into it; otherwise return every method.
hints: First compute exactly what k can reach; then one edge scan decides whether that whole set is removable.
Use iterative DFS from k, then look for an invocation whose caller is outside and callee inside.
Return all methods on a blocking edge; otherwise filter out the suspicious set.
Reachability defines every required removal, and the edge condition is precisely the stated all-or-nothing external dependency rule.
editorial: Reachability defines every required removal, and the edge condition is precisely the stated all-or-nothing external dependency rule.

tests.explanation: Outside calls from 0 and 3 enter the suspicious set, so no method is removed.
Methods 0,1,2 can be removed, leaving 3 and 4.
